checked.found: -479 is Confucius's death year (traditional anchor). Mainstream scholarship puts compilation across the Warring States to mid-Han; no source dates the compilation to 479 BCE.
Garden founded in Athens c. 307/306 BCE; 306 is the common single date.

Search confirms oldest excavated text (Guodian) dated to about 300 BCE; composition placed in late 4th or early 3rd century BCE, though authorship and exact date are disputed. -300 is approximate but defensible; description makes no date claim.
Britannica places him in the 2nd century CE; conventional range 150 to 250 CE, other scholars 1st to 3rd century. Traditional founder of Madhyamaka. 150 is approximate.
Written in Latin between 397 and 400 CE, 13 books; Augustine was a bishop (of Hippo) at the time.
Sources say begun c. 1014, completed c. 1020, published 1027. 1027 is the publication date, but the description says 'completed'.
Sources place his Longchang enlightenment in 1508, after exile for opposing the eunuch Liu Jin; core teaching is mind is principle.
Published anonymously, Books I and II in 1739 and Book III in 1740, when Hume was in his twenties. Start year 1739 matches.
Published 1792; argues women should receive a rational education and rights comparable to men's.
Published 1807 (Bamberg and Würzburg); traces consciousness toward 'absolute knowing'.
Published 1859; sets out the harm principle.
Britannica: published in four parts 1883 to 1885; contains 'God is dead' and the Overman. Part one is 1883 (from memory, search did not split parts).
Written 13 to 22 November 1909 aboard the Kildonan Castle (about ten days), published in Indian Opinion in December 1909.
First published in German in 1921 (English 1922); concerns the limits of language and calls metaphysical philosophising nonsense.
L'Etre et le neant, 1943. 'Existence precedes essence' is the book's central notion per Wikipedia, though its best-known statement is the 1945 lecture 'Existentialism is a Humanism'. Year is sound.
First published in Paris in 1949; contains 'One is not born, but becomes, a woman'.
Published 1971 by Harvard's Belknap Press; Rawls taught at Harvard from 1962; veil of ignorance confirmed.
